context: Queue task 324, GH#624, stage S5. CODE-DESIGNER committed the design as bbc9af9 on feature/WF02-REQ172-20260828. Hard gate -- do not rubber-stamp. Design's own headline claims to verify against the real installed deps: (1) host-function callbacks run inside the Wasmex instance's own GenServer process, not the caller's task (cited from deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex.ex handle_info/2); (2) three DIFFERENT discard mechanisms across the five failure arms (explicit GenServer.stop for trap/fuel/memory-cap, abandonment for wall-clock timeout per CallTimeout's own disclosed finding, direct process exit/1 for fail) -- verify this isn't papering over a real inconsistency; (3) call_service's missing-capability path fails at INSTANTIATION via REQ-167's existing gate, never reaching guest code, while service failure returns a normal {:ok,...} call with a false envelope -- verify these two shapes are genuinely distinguishable and that no call-time capability re-check was silently assumed instead; (4) fail's uninterceptability rests on exit/1 crashing the same GenServer process the callback runs in -- verify this actually prevents guest code from ever seeing/ignoring a return, and check the design's own OQ-2 (exact crash-shape at GenServer.call boundary) is either resolved or legitimately deferred to ELIXIR-DEV as a live-verify task, not silently assumed; (5) the shared parity harness's exhaustiveness check (scenarios() registry cross-checked against a new CapabilityGate.known_host_functions/0 derived from @known_imports) actually forces a future host function to add a parity case, not merely encourages it; (6) all 5 non-ABI semantic differences enumerated in section 9 are genuinely non-ABI and genuinely justified, not disguised defects; (7) confirm no Lua host-API implementation file is proposed for modification anywhere in the design (the priv/wasm_fixtures/*.wat fixture flagged for update is not a Lua file, confirm that's correct). Verify design contains no implementation code, and every acceptance criterion below is concretely addressable from the design as written.

task.description: Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req172-wasm-host-api-write-path-and-parity-suite.md against every REQ-172 acceptance criterion. This is a hard gate -- if the design has a genuine defect (a false live-verification claim, an unaddressed acceptance criterion, ambiguity that would force ELIXIR-DEV to invent behavior, or implementation code where interface/@spec-level design belongs), send it back to CODE-DESIGNER with the specific defect named, do not approve it.
acceptance_criteria: ONE shared scenario definition is executed against BOTH the Lua executor and the WASM handler, asserting identical observable outcomes -- WASM-12's own acceptance criterion -- rather than two separately written suites; the shared harness is a single named module or fixture, quoted in the moduledoc

a test asserts a guest that writes variables and then FAILS leaves instance variable state unchanged, asserted separately for each failure arm: a guest trap, fuel exhaustion (REQ-169), memory cap (REQ-169), wall-clock timeout (REQ-170), and fail
a test asserts a guest that writes several variables and succeeds applies all of them with no observable partial state

a test asserts call_service returns a structured error to the guest on service failure rather than trapping, and a separate test asserts a missing service capability fails per REQ-167 -- the two behaviours asserted distinctly
a test asserts a guest that attempts to catch or ignore its own fail STILL yields a failed outcome and does not run to completion -- the WASM analogue of REQ-161's uninterceptable-termination test

any semantic difference between the Lua and WASM host APIs that is not purely ABI (string encoding, return shape) is enumerated explicitly in the moduledoc with its justification; the moduledoc states that WASM-12 limits differences to ABI, so an unlisted one means the requirement is unmet

the moduledoc states that the Lua host API is the definition WASM conforms to per decision 0014 Decision (4), and that no Lua-side behaviour was changed to ease parity; confirmed by `git diff --stat` scoped to this requirement's commits showing no Lua host-API implementation file modified
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
